name: Hanno Renner
profile: German entrepreneur who co-founded HR-software company Personio in Munich in 2015 with fellow CDTM classmates. Personio grew into one of Europe's most valuable startups (valued ~$8B in 2022), serving SMEs with HR and payroll software; Renner continues to lead it as CEO.
interesting_fact: Personio started with about $200 in the bank and reached a $6.3B valuation within six years, making Renner one of Europe's youngest unicorn CEOs.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Personio he trained as a sailing skipper and spent semester breaks taking tourists out on sailing boats; he studied industrial engineering at HTWG Konstanz and Management & Technology at TUM.
notes: Press releases also list press@personio.de; best route is Personio's comms team.

name: Lisa Riolo
profile: Affiliate-marketing veteran who was SVP of Business Development at Commission Junction before co-founding Impact Radius (now impact.com) in Santa Barbara in 2008. impact.com became a leading partnership-automation platform valued at ~$2B+; Riolo is described as co-founder and advisor and remains an industry speaker.
interesting_fact: She has 25+ years in affiliate/partnership marketing and was among impact.com's 2008 founding team alongside Per Pettersen, Roger Kjensrud, Todd Crawford and Wade Crang.
deep_cut_fact: Mixergy's Andrew Warner titled his interview with her 'The woman who paid me $1 million in affiliate revenue' from her Commission Junction days; she also co-founded workzones, a Santa Barbara co-working business.
notes: Low public profile; current operating role at impact.com unclear (listed as co-founder/advisor). Workzones detail is from Crunchbase bio.

name: Tilli Kalisky-Bannett
current_role: Managing Partner, Pinegrove Venture Partners (formerly SVB Capital); co-founder, At-Bay
profile: Venture investor and co-founder of At-Bay, the cyber-insurance insurtech founded in 2016 and valued at ~$1.35B. She spent about 10 years as a partner at Greylock IL (now 83North) backing European and Israeli startups and now co-leads Pinegrove, a ~$10B multi-strategy venture platform spun out of SVB Capital.
interesting_fact: At-Bay, which she co-founded, insures companies against losses from cyberattacks and made the Forbes Fintech 50 in 2023 and 2024, with 35,000+ policyholders.
deep_cut_fact: Before investing she earned a magna cum laude BA in Psychology at Hebrew University, then an MBA at MIT; she now lives in Palo Alto.
notes: Investor-founder rather than At-Bay operator; one source says she is not in an active At-Bay leadership role. Best route is via Pinegrove (general inquiries address). Milken Global Conference 2025 speaker.

name: Darpan Sanghvi
current_role: Founder, CoFounder Circle (AI-native startup acceleration/venture studio platform, India)
profile: Mumbai-based entrepreneur who founded MyGlamm in 2015 and built it into the Good Glamm Group, a content-to-commerce beauty conglomerate valued at $1.2B in 2021 (backers incl. Warburg Pincus, L'Occitane, Amazon). After the group was broken up by lenders in 2025, he launched CoFounder Circle, an AI-native accelerator for startups and MSMEs, and judges on JioHotstar's 'Pitch To Get Rich'.
interesting_fact: He is credited with pioneering the 'content-to-commerce' model in India's beauty industry, buying media/influencer platforms POPxo, Plixxo and ScoopWhoop to sell MyGlamm products; the group later launched Wyn Beauty with Serena Williams.
deep_cut_fact: While studying engineering at MIT Pune he worked at Baazee.com, the Indian auction site later bought by eBay; he later did a dual MBA at ESADE (Barcelona) and UT Austin.
notes: Sensitive: Good Glamm Group collapsed in July 2025; he pledged part of future earnings/CoFounder Circle equity to make stakeholders whole. Avoid as an opener. Likely official site cofoundercircle.com (unconfirmed link to him); LinkedIn is his main public channel.

name: Ornit Dweck-Maizel
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Technology Officer, Sunbit (Los Angeles / Tel Aviv)
profile: Israeli-born fintech engineer who co-founded buy-now-pay-later company Sunbit in 2016 with Arad Levertov and Tal Riesenfeld. As CTO she built the technology that lets dental offices, auto service departments and retailers offer instant point-of-sale financing; Sunbit was valued at ~$1.1B in 2021. Earlier she worked at Intel, SuperDerivatives and as VP R&D at Whipclip.
interesting_fact: Sunbit's financing is offered in roughly one in six US auto dealership service departments.
deep_cut_fact: With no offices at the start, she held Sunbit's first engineering team meeting in her in-laws' backyard garage at the end of a dirt road; after working late the team walked out by phone flashlight over rain-soaked mud.
notes: Also known as Ornit Maizel. Degrees: BSc Information Systems Engineering (Ben-Gurion Univ.), MBA in Finance (Tel Aviv Univ.). Mentors startups.

name: Paulo Marques
profile: Portuguese computer scientist (PhD, University of Coimbra) who co-founded Feedzai with Nuno Sebastião and Pedro Bizarro; Feedzai builds real-time machine-learning fraud and financial-crime detection used by major banks and payment firms. He served as CTO for about 13 years and is now Technical Fellow; Feedzai was valued at $2B+ in an October 2025 round.
interesting_fact: Feedzai, which he co-founded in Coimbra, was selected by the European Central Bank to provide fraud & risk management for the forthcoming digital euro.
deep_cut_fact: Before Feedzai he spent six years as an expert technical consultant at the European Space Agency's operations centre (ESOC) in Darmstadt, while also teaching as an assistant professor at Coimbra and directing CMU Portugal's professional master in software.
notes: Full name Paulo Jorge Pimenta Marques. Academic and technical profile; author of 40+ peer-reviewed papers; Forbes Technology Council member.

name: Benjamin Eldridge
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Technology Officer, Nutcracker Therapeutics (Emeryville, CA)
profile: Engineer-inventor who co-founded Nutcracker Therapeutics in 2018 with former FormFactor CEO Igor Khandros, applying semiconductor-style biochip manufacturing to RNA therapeutics. Previously a longtime FormFactor executive (incl. CTO) after starting at IBM's T.J. Watson Research Center. Nutcracker has repositioned as an RNA contract research/development/manufacturing (CRDMO) business.
interesting_fact: Nutcracker's ACORN/NMU systems make nanoparticle-encapsulated RNA therapeutics on single-use biochips, essentially an RNA factory 'in a box' borrowed from chip-industry thinking.
deep_cut_fact: He is a named inventor on more than 200 US patents, and began his career doing engineering at IBM's T.J. Watson Research Center; he holds an M.S. in Physics from Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute.
notes: Company status unclear: CEO Khandros retired March 2025 (Cynthia Collins interim CEO); PitchBook lists company out of business as of Nov 2025, while GEN covered it in Dec 2025. Verify his current role before outreach. No published press contact found.

name: Alexandre Cognard
current_role: CTO (and co-founder), Arianee (Paris) - digital product passport / blockchain infrastructure
profile: French technologist who co-founded Paris luxury resale marketplace Vestiaire Collective in 2009 and served as its CTO; Vestiaire later reached a ~$1.7B+ valuation with Kering among its backers. He then co-founded Arianee (2018), where as CTO he leads protocol R&D for digital product passports used by luxury and retail brands.
interesting_fact: Arianee says it operates more than 4 million digital product passports for brands such as Breitling, Fnac Darty and Mugler.
deep_cut_fact: Vestiaire Collective began life as 'Vestiaire de Copines' (roughly 'girlfriends' wardrobe'), a virtual consignment site that raised EUR400k in Oct 2009 and a first EUR1.5M round from Ventech in 2010; Cognard and Christian Jorge gave FrenchWeb an early video interview as co-founders.
notes: Low-profile technical founder; best route is via Arianee (general contact address). Arianee's site lists him as CTO; third-party sites list him as co-founder.

name: John Hodges
current_role: Head of Film, Jax Media (per Disney bio); co-founder of A24 (exited 2018)
profile: Film producer who co-founded indie studio A24 in 2012 with Daniel Katz and David Fenkel, helping steer acquisitions/distribution for 70+ films including Moonlight, Lady Bird and Ex Machina, and launching its TV arm in 2015. He left A24 in 2018 (A24 later valued at ~$3.5B) and joined Jax Media in 2019, where he leads feature film development and production.
interesting_fact: Before A24 he ran production and development at Big Beach, the company behind 'Little Miss Sunshine'.
deep_cut_fact: A Georgetown College grad (C'00), he credits Big Beach's Peter Saraf as his biggest influence for teaching him 'what it truly means to be a producer' and giving him the confidence to start A24; his Georgetown haunts were Cactus Cantina and Quick Pita.
notes: Exec producer of Disney's 'The Slumber Party' (2023). Very low public profile; no published contact found—route via Jax Media or reps. Current Jax role should be re-confirmed.

name: Evan Loomis
current_role: General Partner, Overmatch Ventures (Austin); co-founder of ICON and Saturn Five
profile: Austin entrepreneur and former Wall Street investment banker who co-founded ICON (with Jason Ballard and Alex Le Roux), the 3D-printed-construction company that printed the first permitted US 3D-printed home and works with NASA on lunar habitats. He also co-founded Saturn Five and now co-leads Overmatch Ventures, which closed a $250M Fund II in March 2026 for early-stage defense, space and deep tech.
interesting_fact: ICON 3D-printed the first permitted home in the US and partnered with NASA on technology for building habitats on the Moon.
deep_cut_fact: He co-wrote 'Get Backed' (Harvard Business Review Press, 2015) with Evan Baehr, a step-by-step guide to raising early-stage capital, and earlier co-founded TreeHouse, an Austin sustainable home-improvement retailer (2010).
notes: Highly relevant to an energy/infra/defense-tech podcast; Texas A&M Mays Business School grad (2003); Kauffman Fellow. Best route: Overmatch general inbox.

name: Wei Deng
profile: Former corporate lawyer (Davis Polk) and banker (Moelis) who founded Clipboard Health in 2016 and took it through Y Combinator (W17). Clipboard runs a marketplace matching nurses and caregivers with shifts at nursing homes and other facilities, reaching a $1B+ valuation in 2022; she co-leads it as Co-CEO.
interesting_fact: She has said she aims to help people climb the socioeconomic ladder; Clipboard's mission is to 'Uplift as Many Communities as Possible', and features like Instant Pay came from staying close to its nurse users.
deep_cut_fact: To 'viscerally experience everything our nurses do', she earned a CNA (certified nursing assistant) certification; in the earliest days she was personally 'the app, our support team, our billing team—all at once.'
notes: Child of immigrants; Pear VC healthcare advisor. Company rebranded web presence to clipboard.com.

name: Sonia Ben-Yehuda
profile: Could not identify this person. Chief (the $1B+ New York private network for senior women executives, launched 2019) is consistently reported as co-founded by Carolyn Childers and Lindsay Kaplan; no source links anyone named Sonia Ben-Yehuda to Chief or to any other company called Chief.
notes: Likely a data error in the input list (name/company mismatch). Web searches for the exact name returned no relevant person. Verify the source record before any outreach.

name: Eliseo Diaz
current_role: Co-founder & Executive Vice President, Flash (FlashParking), Austin TX (titles vary by source: EVP International Markets / CRO)
profile: Austin entrepreneur who co-founded FlashParking in 2011 with Juan Rodriguez and Dean Cleaver. Flash grew from a valet-payments app into a parking and mobility technology platform (cloud parking access/revenue control, EV and curb management), valued at ~$1B+ and raising $85M in 2024; Diaz has led sales, marketing and international expansion.
interesting_fact: Flash started as 'Flash Valet' after the founders noticed how hard it was to summon a valet and tip from a phone; it let customers request their car and pay/tip via text.
deep_cut_fact: Before Flash he worked in fintech and telecom, including Rêv Worldwide, NetSpend and Telcordia, and is listed as having served in the U.S. Army.
notes: Full name Eliseo J. Diaz. Low public profile; Juan Rodriguez is the company's public face. Army/prior-employer detail is from an aggregator (CB Insights) — verify before using.

name: Matt Barnard
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, One Unlimited / One Bio (fiber science platform; GoodVice consumer brand)
profile: Entrepreneur who co-founded indoor vertical-farming company Plenty in 2014 with Nate Storey, raising $900M+ (SoftBank, Walmart) and reaching a ~$2B valuation; he stepped from CEO to executive chairman in 2022. In 2023 he became co-founder & CEO of One Bio, a UC Davis spinout making imperceptible high-dose plant fiber from ag side-streams, which raised a $27M Series A in Dec 2024.
interesting_fact: One Bio's first ingredient is an oat-derived fiber that is flavorless, odorless, colorless and water-soluble, so it can be added to foods at unusually high doses; backers include Leaps by Bayer, Mitsui and DSM.
deep_cut_fact: He argues health shouldn't depend on discipline, summed up in his line 'Virtuous suffering is a system failure.'
notes: Avoid leading with Plenty's later history (company was reported to have restructured in 2025; not re-verified here). A single profile says he was raised on a Wisconsin cherry/apple farm—unverified, not used. Web search budget ran out mid-research.

name: Sam Blackshear
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Mysten Labs (developer of the Sui blockchain)
profile: Programming-languages engineer who created the Move smart-contract language while at Meta's Diem (Libra) payments project. In September 2021 he co-founded Mysten Labs with Evan Cheng, Adeniyi Abiodun, George Danezis and Kostas Chalkias; it raised $36M led by a16z, then $300M at a ~$2B valuation, and launched the Sui Layer-1 blockchain.
interesting_fact: Move, the language he created for Diem, was designed to avoid classes of smart-contract bugs common in Ethereum's Solidity; it now powers Sui and Aptos.
deep_cut_fact: Before Meta he earned his PhD in the University of Colorado Boulder's Programming Languages and Verification (PLV) group, where he is listed among the PhD alumni.
notes: 'Sui' comes from the Japanese/Chinese character for water. No published press email found on Mysten/Sui sites (JS-rendered); best route likely via Mysten Labs or Sui Foundation comms. Web search budget ran out, so contacts are thin.

name: Francis Duong
current_role: Co-founder & Advisor, Flexe; co-founder, Formational (since Aug 2022)
profile: Seattle-area technologist who co-founded Flexe in 2013 and served as its CTO; Flexe runs an on-demand warehousing and fulfillment network for retailers, valued at ~$1B+ after its 2022 raise. He now advises Flexe and since 2022 has been co-founding Formational, focused on reimagining e-commerce.
interesting_fact: Flexe pioneered an 'Airbnb for warehouses' model, letting retailers rent spare warehouse capacity on demand instead of signing long leases.
deep_cut_fact: Before Flexe he co-founded AppRebates (2009–2015), a Y Combinator-backed service that helped iPhone developers market their apps, and earlier built mobile social-networking features at IceBreaker.
notes: Very low public profile. flexe.com blocked automated fetch, so no press contact retrieved; route via Flexe comms or LinkedIn. Web search budget ran out; career details from TheOrg profile.
